answer: Proposed rule: a basalt registry admits one reward key per manufacturer-certified secure-element die, with its kernel hash pinned. Verifiers broadcast a fresh whisper nonce and demand simultaneous die-signed responses; a reused serial or missed probe forfeits that epoch’s pay. A farm can rent chips, its cheapest bypass, but each added identity still needs its own live die for the whole epoch; one chip cannot back two keys. The registry checks serial collisions and signatures, assuming the chip issuer does not forge serials.
